clue.text: Ginger photographer shoots fish

parts.note: ginger hair is red, so the colour word supplies the first piece
a snapper is informal slang for a photographer, especially a press one

explanation.surface: A red-haired photographer takes pictures of fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shoots' looks like the photographer's verb, but it only links the wordplay to the definition at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The red snapper is a reddish sea fish of warm waters, prized for eating.

clue.text: Rescue vessel represents a good deal

explanation.surface: A lifeboat stands for a bargain.
explanation.definitionFit: A raft is a flat floating craft used to escape a wreck, and 'a raft of' is an idiom for a large quantity.

clue.text: Clammy part of Rwandan kingdom

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some damp and humid region of a central African country.
explanation.definitionFit: Dank and clammy both describe unpleasantly cold, moist air or surfaces.

clue.text: Condition may be dwarfed by gran's philosophy

parts.note: nan is an affectionate British name for a grandmother, as gran is
an ism is any doctrine or school of thought, a philosophy

explanation.surface: A medical state that could seem small beside grandma's outlook on life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'May be dwarfed by' joins the definition to the wordplay while hinting at what the condition is.
explanation.definitionFit: Nanism is the medical term for abnormally short stature, i.e. dwarfism.

clue.text: Personal effects of a soldier of fortune

parts.note: a private is a soldier of the lowest rank
a fortune is wealth or possessions, one's property

explanation.surface: The belongings left behind by a mercenary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soldier of fortune' reads as one phrase meaning a mercenary; split it and each half gives a piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Things owned by an individual rather than the state, such as clothing and belongings, count as one's own possessions.

clue.text: Points to list with recruit

parts.note: E and N stand for east and north, two points of the compass
a roll is a list of names, as in a roll call

explanation.surface: Someone directs a newcomer towards a register.
explanation.walkthrough: This is the American spelling; British usage has one L.
explanation.definitionFit: To recruit someone is to sign them up as a member, putting their name on the books.

clue.text: Well known like he played tennis long ago

definitions.text: Well known like he played tennis long ago

parts.note: as means like, in the sense of 'such as' or 'in the way that'
taken as written

explanation.surface: A famous figure from tennis history.
explanation.walkthrough: Arthur Ashe was an American player who won Wimbledon in 1975; the whole clue describes him while AS and HE build the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Ashe, a celebrated US tennis champion of the 1960s and 70s, fits a famous player from the past.

clue.text: Racing fish used by winter sportsman

parts.note: racing is about speed, so the adjective is rendered by that noun
a skate is a flat cartilaginous sea fish like a ray

explanation.surface: A fast fish being handled by someone on the ice slopes.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is elliptical: '(something) used by winter sportsman', the long-bladed boot worn on an ice oval.
explanation.definitionFit: A speed skate is the long-bladed boot worn by a competitor in ice-rink racing, a winter event.

clue.text: I represent new format of endeavour

indicators.note: putting the words into a new format means rearranging their letters

explanation.surface: Someone says they stand for a fresh way of attempting things.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of I REPRESENT are rearranged under 'new format of'.
explanation.definitionFit: Enterprise is a bold undertaking or project, an endeavour.

clue.text: Is francine messing about with moneymen

indicators.note: messing about suggests the letters are jumbled up playfully

explanation.surface: A woman called Francine is fooling around with bankers.
explanation.walkthrough: IS FRANCINE has exactly the ten letters wanted, rearranged under 'messing about'.
explanation.definitionFit: Financiers are people who manage or provide large sums of money, a financial elite.

clue.text: A talent for being crooked

explanation.surface: Someone has a gift for dishonesty.
explanation.definitionFit: A bent is a natural aptitude or inclination, and bent is also slang for corrupt or dishonest, as well as literally curved.

clue.text: Temperate mob at issue rioting

indicators.note: rioting implies wild disorder, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A restrained crowd turns violent over a dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: MOB AT ISSUE gives ten letters that 'rioting' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Abstemious means sparing with food and especially drink, moderate in indulgence.

clue.text: Giant upset in sea vessel

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters within the word for sea

parts.note: brine is salt water, a poetic word for the sea

indicators.note: upset means knocked over or disturbed, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A huge figure is knocked over in a seafaring boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sea vessel' reads as one phrase, but 'sea' is wordplay and only 'vessel' defines; 'upset' scrambles the giant and 'in' puts the result inside the salt water.
explanation.definitionFit: A brigantine is a two-masted sailing ship, a type of seagoing craft.

clue.text: May go with a battery case to make a charge

definitions.text: May go with a battery case to make a charge

parts.words: May go with a battery case to make a charge
parts.note: battery here is the legal offence, often paired with an attack threat in one criminal charge, not an electrical cell

explanation.surface: Something that could pair with a power cell to build up electrical charge.
explanation.walkthrough: Battery and charge both suggest electricity, but in law 'assault and battery' is a single criminal charge.
explanation.definitionFit: In law an attack or threat of violence is commonly charged together with battery, the actual blow.

clue.text: Battle you end in offers lots

indicators.note: to end up in something is to be placed inside it

parts.note: action is fighting, as in soldiers seeing action in battle
U is text-speak for you

explanation.surface: Fighting finishes up with you being in a sale of many items.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a verb phrase standing for 'a sale that offers lots', items bid for one by one.
explanation.definitionFit: At a public sale goods called lots are put up one after another for bidders.

clue.text: Childs game a branch of Filipino language

parts.note: tag is a playground chasing game
a log is a cut length of tree branch or trunk

explanation.surface: A playground game turns out to be a dialect of the Philippines.
explanation.definitionFit: Tagalog is the main tongue of the Philippines, the basis of the national language Filipino.

clue.text: Elementary meal taken inside can be seen

definitions.text: Elementary meal taken inside can be seen

parts.words: Elementary meal taken inside can be seen
parts.note: a chemical element swallowed in a drink before an X-ray, so that the gut shows up on the image

explanation.surface: A simple dinner eaten indoors is visible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elementary' means a chemical element, and a patient swallows a barium meal so the digestive tract shows on X-ray.
explanation.definitionFit: Barium is a metallic element whose sulphate, drunk as a 'meal', is opaque to X-rays.

clue.text: Last real snake to run

indicators.note: last here picks only the final letter of the word that follows it

parts.note: the adder is a venomous snake, the viper native to Britain

explanation.surface: In a board game, the final snake leads to a climbing aid.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes snakes and ladders; 'run' means a tear in tights, which British English calls a ladder. The adder is Britain's native venomous snake.
explanation.definitionFit: A ladder in stockings or tights is a vertical line of unravelled stitches, which Americans call a run.

clue.text: Telegraph work it offers a circus a line

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Telegraph work it offers a circus a line', anagrams TELEGRAPH WORK IT to the answer but has no anagram indicator and no sound definition; it looks garbled and no source gives the original.
annotationWithheld.clue: Telegraph work it offers a circus a line

clue.text: "30 seconds" charged bit to flunkey

parts.note: thirty seconds is half a minute, and half the word minute gives the letters needed
an ion is an atom or molecule carrying an electric charge

explanation.surface: Half a minute's charge is paid to a servant.
explanation.walkthrough: '30 seconds' is half of MINUTE, so its first half, MIN, is taken.
explanation.definitionFit: A minion is a servile follower or underling, like a lackey.

clue.text: Character gets tan over Yorkshire river

indicators.note: in a down clue over means turned upwards, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
the Ure is a river in North Yorkshire, England

explanation.surface: Someone's personality changes after sunbathing beside a northern river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' reverses TAN to give NAT.
explanation.definitionFit: One's nature is one's basic temperament or disposition, the same as personality.

clue.text: Large vessels in which to cook a roast

indicators.note: to cook something can mean to falsify it, so the letters are doctored into a new order

explanation.surface: Big pots for preparing a Sunday joint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' rearranges A ROAST; 'vessels' means blood vessels, not cooking pots.
explanation.definitionFit: The aorta is the body's main artery carrying blood from the heart, the largest blood vessel.

clue.text: It stops the liner from moving

definitions.text: It stops the liner from moving

parts.words: It stops the liner from moving
parts.note: a liner here is a large passenger ship, held in place by a heavy hooked weight dropped to the seabed

explanation.surface: Something prevents an ocean liner from going anywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy iron weight lowered to the sea floor holds a ship in place.

clue.text: Sleeping child taken off from abduction

indicators.note: taken off from means the shorter word is removed from the longer one

parts.note: kidnapping is the abduction of a person
a kid is a child

explanation.surface: A dozing infant is rescued from kidnappers.
explanation.walkthrough: KID is removed from KIDNAPPING, leaving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Napping means taking a short sleep, dozing.

clue.text: God makes duck noise

parts.note: a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so it gives the letter shaped like zero
din is a loud continuous noise

explanation.surface: A deity produces a quacking sound.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a duck is a batsman's score of zero, hence O.
explanation.definitionFit: Odin is the chief deity of Norse mythology.

clue.text: Noble John Wayne

explanation.surface: A Hollywood cowboy is called aristocratic.
explanation.definitionFit: A duke is the highest rank of the British peerage, and 'The Duke' was the screen actor's lifelong nickname.

clue.text: Kettle of fish for dining hall

explanation.surface: A pan of fish is served in the canteen.
explanation.definitionFit: 'A pretty kettle of fish' is an idiom for a muddle, and a military mess is where officers eat together.

clue.text: With this, army watchmen are content

definitions.text: With this, army watchmen are content

parts.words: With this, army watchmen are content
parts.note: content can be read as contained, so the military sentries are held within a building

explanation.surface: Soldiers on watch are satisfied with something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Content' looks like happy, but read it as contained: the building holds the sentries.
explanation.definitionFit: A building where military sentries are stationed or prisoners held under watch.

clue.text: Piglets, you first replaced quietly for American city-types

indicators.note: replaced means one letter is swapped out for another in the phrase

parts.note: piglets are new porkers, young pigs being fattened
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning quietly

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of the word it follows

explanation.surface: Young pigs are swapped for Manhattan residents.
explanation.walkthrough: In NEW PORKERS the P (quietly) is replaced by Y, the first letter of 'you'.
explanation.definitionFit: Residents of the largest US metropolis are known by that city's name.
